findings.quote: void notify(`Open ${challenge.verificationUri} and enter the code ${challenge.userCode}`).catch(() => undefined);
findings.problem: A failure to send the challenge message to Telegram is swallowed with no comment. If the notify fails, the user never sees the code, the login waits out the full 10-minute limit and then reports only "Device login timed out".
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the swallow (an unhandled rejection would be worse) but add a comment saying why, and either abort the login on a failed notify or record the failure so endedEarly can say "could not send the code".

findings.problem: The code relies on ordering inside one closure: a comment at 3591-3592 says "(before `surface` is assigned)", `focusApplied` (3616) guards a first paint that may run before `surface` exists, and `finish` (3368-3374) and `switchTab` (3448-3452) both use `surface?.`. The `const surface: TabbedSurface | undefined = openTabbedSurface(...)` at 3619 is typed as possibly undefined only to satisfy those earlier references.
findings.suggested_fix: Part of the CC-1 extraction: pass the surface into paint/finish explicitly, or create the surface first and fill in the paint callback afterwards.

findings.problem: openTabbedSurface duplicates the ModalHost key handling (Esc, x, Tab, digit keys) for its full-screen fallback; the Tab cycle is written twice in the same function (claimKey at ~2278 and `cycle` at ~2347).
findings.suggested_fix: Make `cycle` the single implementation and call it from claimKey; share the key table between the two branches.

findings.problem: createRemoteDeviceLogin.connect is about 47 lines with a nested ternary in endedEarly (`timedOut ? ... : stoppedByCaller ? ... : ...`). The LOGIN_* constants (84-87) cover some messages, but four sentences are inline (115, 131-ish, 148, 152).
findings.suggested_fix: Turn the outcome into a small `endReason()` function with if/return, and move the inline sentences next to the other LOGIN_* constants.

findings.quote: async function runTest(tabId: ProvidersTabId, name: string): Promise<void> {
findings.problem: Provider [Test] has no in-flight guard, on either surface. In the Providers dialog, Enter or a click on [Test] calls runTest(...) every time; a second press before the first probe returns starts a second concurrent GET /models (and a second model-profile store refresh through onSummary) for the same provider, and whichever resolves last writes the row's status, so a slow first probe can overwrite a newer result. Telegram's [Test] (testProvider -> testProviderForRemote -> probeProviderConnection) likewise starts one probe per tap, with no per-provider dedup.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a Map<providerId, Promise<ProviderProbeOutcome>> of probes in flight (one in the dialog step, one in the Telegram hook) and return the existing promise for a repeat press; delete the entry in finally. Or ignore the press while statuses holds the 'testing…' content for that row.

findings.problem: testAddable awaits host.testProvider, and pickAddableProvider awaits host.listAddableProviders, with no try/catch. connectAddable, in the same class, wraps host.connectWithDeviceLogin in try/catch and answers with a fixed sentence. If either unguarded hook rejects, the rejection reaches detach()'s `.catch(() => undefined)`, so the topic gets no reply and `ended(end, ...)` is never called.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the testProvider and listAddableProviders calls like connectAddable does. On a throw, reply with a fixed sentence such as 'Test failed. The details are in the shell.' and return "failed". Never put the error message in the reply.

findings.problem: runProvidersModal decides 'connected' from `failure === undefined && models.length > 0`. For a provider that providerByName does not know, resolveModelsForPicker returns `{ models: [...provider.models], source: "fallback" }` with no failure, so the check passes without any /models call. The same condition guards both the connect branch and the custom branch. Reproducible path: Connected tab, Disconnect a custom provider (removeCustomCompatProvider); switch to Add provider (the `all` snapshot is not pruned in armOrConfirmDisconnect, so the removed provider is still listed); [Connect] it; the base-URL step writes an orphan baseUrls override; the picker falls back to the stale provider.models; the modal shows 'connected - N model(s)' and upserts a phantom row on the Connected tab. Picking that row would switch the session to a provider that no longer exists. Non-registry providers (e.g. ollama, anthropic) take the same path, whereas Add-tab [Test] answers 'unknown provider - cannot test' for them, so the two buttons disagree.
findings.suggested_fix: Require `result.models.source === "live"` (or re-check providerByName) before marking the provider connected, in both the connect and custom branches. Also drop the provider from `all` when disconnectProvider returns kind `custom`, so the Add tab cannot offer a removed provider.

findings.problem: In 'the typed key is on no channel the shell shows' the test mounts selectProviderModelInTui directly, never the /connect handler inside launchTuiAgentShell (tui-shell.ts:10436) that is the code which toasts, prints system lines and writes the transcript. So transcriptText(h.chrome) not containing the key, and the toast/status/header/title spy collecting nothing secret, only prove that the picker function itself does not write there; the shell-side half is not exercised. Also `expect(existsSync(configDir)).toBe(true)` is true by construction (mkdtempSync in beforeEach), and `expect(settled).toBe(true)` at line 367 directly follows `await pending` and is tautological.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the tautological assertions, and either narrow the test title to 'the picker writes the key to no chrome channel' or add a source-text audit like the AC7 block in connect-provider-buttons.test.ts for the /connect handler. AC7's journal and flow-log clauses are verified by no test in this slice at all (see F-002).

findings.problem: createConnectedProvidersCache stamps `at: now()` when the load STARTS and treats an entry older than ttlMs (15s) as expired even while its promise is still pending. The probe behind it (filterConnectedDetectedProviders) is a sequential `for ... await fetchOpenAiCompatModelsDetailed` loop, one /models request per keyed provider, each bounded only by MODELS_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS. If a burst's load takes longer than 15s (several slow or timing-out providers), the second call of the burst (listProviders then listAddableProviders) finds the entry 'expired', starts a second full sequential probe in parallel with the first, and the 'one probe serves both' claim in the doc comment does not hold.
findings.suggested_fix: Stamp the TTL when the load RESOLVES, and while an entry's promise is pending always return it: keep `entry = { at: Infinity, value }` until it settles, then set `at = now()` in a `.then`. The failed-load eviction already handles the error path.
